answer: Bond curve: each new agent locks a POA bond priced at 2^k units, where k is how many agents the same funding source already registered this epoch. The attacker pays every bond, so the tenth fake identity costs 512x the first, piling up like a dune. Failure case: a farm that splits funds through mixers still leaves karst-like gaps, since unexplained deposits get audited and a failed audit slashes the bond into a canyon.
